recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-23066 unless the Security WG later changes the underlying AuditEvent.action policy for search/query events.
issue_request: FHIR-23066 was a Published/Persuasive Security WG change request for R5 asking FHIR-core AuditEvent to explain why query/search audit events use AuditEvent.action = Execute rather than Read despite REST searches often using HTTP GET.
initial_application: No local git commit with FHIR-23066 in the subject or body was found, but the Jira comment links HL7/fhir pull request 708. Local commit 8f93636e058fa1a4b9ce4240fea41076e10e6760 added exactly the requested sentence to source/auditevent/auditevent-notes.xml on 2019-10-03, and current blame still attributes the sentence to that commit.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists auditevent=AuditEvent as an active resource. Later related work, especially FHIR-26938, added a Recording Search Events subsection that repeats the same Execute rationale for search requests; FHIR-37820 clarified the Read action definition without changing the Execute definition for query/search operations. The cited Zulip thread supports keeping query/search as Execute for ATNA/DICOM consistency and because searches execute parameters rather than retrieve a single identified object. No Confluence reference for FHIR-23066 was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because active source/auditevent/auditevent-notes.xml already implements the FHIR-23066 resolution and no additional source change is necessary.

related_jiras.note: Added broader Recording Search Events guidance for GET/POST searches and repeats the same Execute rationale; it is already represented on the combined branch.

Earlier AuditEvent guidance mapped search, search-type, and search-system REST interactions to Execute.
Duplicate companion found in Jira search for FHIR-37820, not an independent reconciliation target.
